references.text: Abraham answers Isaac that God himself will provide the lamb for the burnt offering – a direct answer to Isaac's question in verse 7.
God provides a ram to be sacrificed in Isaac's place, fulfilling the event Isaac asks about in verse 7.
Noah builds an altar and offers a burnt offering to the Lord – an early example of a burnt offering (עֹלָה) like the one Isaac asks about.
The prophecy concerning the Lord's suffering servant as a lamb led to slaughter – a typological connection to Isaac's question about the lamb for the burnt offering.
The Letter to the Hebrews refers directly to Abraham's faith and actions in connection with the sacrifice of Isaac.
John points to Jesus as 'the Lamb of God who takes away the sin of the world' – a typological fulfillment of the lamb Isaac asked about.
Contrast between Isaac's trust in God's provision and Isaac's blindness that allows himself to be deceived.
The same dialogue form is used to reveal truth (22:7) and to lie (27:18).
Contrast between Isaac's faith in God's provision in the fire and the rich man's despair in the fire.
Contrast between Isaac's clear senses at the moment of faith and his failing senses during the deception.
Parallel in the response of obedience: the father answers God's call, the son answers the father's call.
Contrast between the son's total surrender (22:7) and the son's deception (27:10) using the same dialogue.
